behavior.arguments: rdi points at a two-word cursor/limit pair: *(rdi) is the cursor, *(rdi+8) is the limit; no other argument is read
behavior.branch_order: entry je to the zero-return when cursor == limit; first iteration advances the cursor slot before checking the node, then checks tag == 2 and first byte == 0, then returns 1 when the advance lands on the limit; later iterations check the previous advance as the node and loop back to the limit compare
behavior.cursor_mutation: *(rdi) becomes (node+0x38) mod 2^64 before node checks; a failing return leaves it at that advance. On a 1 return the cursor equals the entry-loaded limit; on entry-equal return the cursor is unchanged.
behavior.loop_invariant: Nodes advance in 0x38 steps modulo 2^64 from the entry cursor. Every checked node must have byte +9 == 2 and byte +0 == 0 to continue. The only limit comparison is equality; there is no ordered bounds check. The limit itself is not dereferenced.
behavior.model_scope: The helper assumes cursor-store memory does not overlap node fields. The original instructions retain the ordered store/read semantics; caller aliasing and mapped-address invariants remain unknown.
behavior.output_shape: rax is fully determined (eax is zeroed on the entry-equal path and at the first iteration before any return, and sete only sets the low byte): 0 or 1, then ret
behavior.termination: The only bound comparison is equality with the entry-loaded limit. A limit unreachable by +0x38 modulo 2^64 does not terminate an all-passing walk; failures or memory faults can terminate separately. The Python step cap bounds the helper only.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, no runtime rebase

naming_relocation.note: no relocation record of any type in any .rela.* section names this window as addend (full-section scan); the absence of a naming relocation does not identify the window's provenance
